title: Мятеж на флоте
desc:
Революционная организация флота (Organização Revolucionária da Armada) устроила мятеж в нашем ВМФ, посадив под арест нескольких офицеров. Целью этого мятежа, возглавляемого командой эсминца «Дао», был поход к испанским портам в Средиземном море и участие в испанской гражданской войне на стороне республиканцев. 

Однако нерешительность некоторых членов команды мешает мятежникам развернуться в полную силу, так что у нас ещё есть возможность остановить их.

title: Стражи паломнического пути
desc:
Each year, thousands of Catholic faithful undertake a pilgrimage to our lands, as the faithful flock to the shrine of Saint James, one of the twelve apostles of Jesus, in a pilgrimage known as the Camino de Santiago. However, as Iberia endures turbulent times, many find themselves at risk should they choose to undertake the pilgrimage. The long journey to Santiago de Compostela has become a treacherous one.

Pilgrims now speak of a seemingly connected group of individuals who stand watch over the pilgrimage route throughout northern Iberia. Many pilgrims simply refer to them as "The Guardians." What appears to be a collection of Catholic faithful housewives and older men, they draw much of their support from local priests and churches along the pilgrimage route. Pilgrims claim that, along their journeys, these Guardians have taken them into their homes, fed them, tended to ill pilgrims, and at times have even provided extended armed escorts to deter ill-doers. Whilst reports do claim that some of these Guardians are armed, they are not considered to be a paramilitary. They appear to have no goal or agenda other than to shepherd the guide to safety in Santiago de Compostela.

title: Патруль на Берегу Смерти
desc:
A brisk wind rolls over the open seas, as a lone vessel of the Galician Coastal Patrol casually navigates the black waters of the night. Three crewmen of this meager vessel sit amongst the company of one another within the claustrophobic crew quarters, huddled around the feeble electric light that the quarters provide in these dark hours. The men pass around an unlabelled bottle of a heavy homemade brandy, taking turns downing a mouthful of the sweet and fiery drink.

"Alright then." belches the youngest of the three, after taking a sizeable swig of brandy. "Now it is your turn. What's the wildest thing you have done on these boring seas?" asks the young man, as he beckons to the oldest among them. "You kids like to hear war stories? Fine. I will entice you." the eldest among them replies. "I was a younger man. In my twenties. Full of life and vigor. I believed in working for my country, and when the opportunity came to do so, I became a seaman. By the time of Franco's coup three decades ago, I was an idealist and a non-commissioned officer. I believed in Franco's coup. In his leadership. So when I learned that the captain of our vessel was a Republican..." The man pauses. "I did not take so kindly to that, and neither did my men. As the captain walked the interior halls of the vessel, my men grabbed him and beat him. Once the Nationalist officers learned that the Republican captain had been captured by the enlisted men, they took charge. They shot the captain, and took command of the vessel in the name of Franco's coup. Back then I felt like a mutinous privateer sailing the Caribbean, but sometimes I now wonder if the world would have been any different if I hadn't sentenced a man to die only for his loyalty to his country." The room falls silent, as the younger men absorb the story they have just been told. "But don't let that give you any ideas!" the older man chimes in. The silence is broken by laughter, as the men begin to pass around their alcohol once again.

title: Служить или не служить?
desc:
Antón strolls down the streets of Santiago, on his way home from his meager job. He does not particularly enjoy his work, yet it allows him to pay for his college education, and with that he is content. Among the city crowds one can spot several men in uniform dotted about. Many young Galician men have enlisted to defend Galicia from the Portuguese and Spanish, who many believe could make a decisive march upon Galicia at any moment. Anton feels inconsequential in the sight of the other boys in uniform. He feels as if they are more important than him. He shies away and continues to proceed down the street on his way home.

As he proceeds through the city, a poster catches his eye. Depicted upon the poster is a soldier with a distinct Spanish uniform, and another with a Portuguese uniform. The third soldier on the poster wears the uniform of a Galician soldier, and stands taller than the Spanish and Portuguese. Underneath the artistic depiction of the soldiers stands a bold, red caption: "Protect our freedom! Enlist today!" Anton stops and ponders the caption. He recalls how insignificant he feels when compared to men in uniform, and for a moment imagines himself as one of those men in uniform. Daydreams cross his mind of becoming a hero of Galicia, fighting bravely to preserve the newly found Galician independence. Wearing his uniform proudly.

Perhaps joining up wouldn't be such a bad idea, he ponders to himself. Sure, he is content with his life as a student, however he imagines that he could be so much more. Mean something to his nation. Make his family proud. Images of grandeur flood his young mind, as he reads the recruitment office address printed on the poster.

title: По стопам предков
desc:
Seven men lay in wait behind various rocks and obstructions by the roadside. Armed with an assortment of French, British, and Spanish muskets, their trap is set. A meager presence patrol of five French soldiers approaches, as the Frenchmen nonchalantly talk amongst one another. The Frenchmen walk right into the guerrilla's kill zone. The frontman of the Galician guerrilla fighters springs out from his cover, and before the French soldiers can react, he fires his weapon. One of the Frenchmen drops to the ground like a ragdoll. With the signal shot having been fired, the other six hidden men rise up quickly, and fire upon their target. Another three Frenchmen drop to the ground. The two surviving French soldiers drop their weapons, and begin to beg in a foreign tongue. The guerrillas, however, show no sympathy, and quickly acquaint the Frenchmen with the cold steel of their bayonets.

Over a century later, at the same narrow road pass, six guerrillas lay behind roadside obstructions. Armed with an assortment of automatic, semi automatic, and bolt action weaponry, they wait for the incoming semi-platoon of Spanish infantrymen to approach. As the Spanish cross the threshold of the Galician guerilla kill zone, an improvised explosive detonates, killing several of the Spanish, and disorienting the rest. Two hand grenades are lobbed, which detonate within the Spanish ranks. Automatic rifle fire opens up from the Galicians, as the surviving Spaniards drop dead.

Much like their Iberian forefathers in the Spanish War of Independence, Galicians fight tooth and nail in the most unconventional ways to stave off occupation and to preserve their independence. No tactic too dirty, no cost too high, these fighters pay the ultimate sacrifice to ensure a future for their nation.

title: Щепотка муки
desc:
On rations, cooking good pasta can be difficult. With this garlic pasta recipe, however, you'll have an easy time making a wholesome and tasty meal for your whole family!

To begin, you will need 1 pound of dried spaghetti noodles.
Then, fill a large pot with water, and apply a teaspoon of salt. Bring the water to a boil.
Place the pasta noodles into the pot.
As the pasta boils, in a separate pan, apply 3 tablespoons of olive oil, and one or two cloves of minced garlic, depending on how much is available in your area. If you have any stale bread, do not put it to waste! Crumble it up and add it to the pan. Apply medium heat.
Once the pasta is prepared in the pot, remove from heat. Apply 1 tablespoon of butter to the pan. Cook until you can clearly smell the minced garlic.
Apply the boiled pasta to the pan. Toss the pasta around thoroughly. If available, sprinkle some cheese in for added flavour!

And there you have it, a tasty meal that fits easily within the parameters of your bi-weekly ration! This guide was designed to feed a family of four, however it can easily be adjusted to feed more, if your family is larger and receives larger rations.

title: Старые друзья
desc:
In the long decades of Franco's rule over Galicia, intellectual thought and ideas were far from encouraged. As the Caudillos' grip over Iberia grew, many Galician intellectuals found themselves facing complete silencing, or should they have resisted, exile. Since the liberation of Galicia, however, many of these intellectuals have trickled back in to Galicia, eager to return to their homeland, free to profess ideas and thoughts without becoming a target.

As a result of the homecoming of the intellectual community, several prominent members of the community have been invited to a public meeting arranged by Álvaro Cunqueiro to discuss important matters held dear by them. Members of the public have arrived in surprising numbers to witness the meeting. The assembly is pitted to contain discussions upon Iberian affairs, the plausibility of the Galician nation, and Iberia's role in the evolving world, among other topics.

The intellectuals, being watched closely by a plethora of citizens and journalists, agree that Galicia has severe challenges facing it outside of pure security matters. The probable economic difficulties that Galicia will face, as well as the geopolitical difficulties of finding and maintaining steady support for such a small nation, are also discussed. As the discussions drag on, many feel a dual sense of liberation and dread. Although finally free, it would appear that the intellectual community, throughout their suppressed years, have developed a rather grim outlook upon Galicia, Iberia, and the world. They profess the dangers of the rapid and evolving new order, and agree that great caution will be needed for Galicia to survive these upcoming tumultuous years.

title: Несколько достойных людей
desc:
"Under the Emergency Public Security Provisions, it is our duty to take you, Miguel Novo, into our custody. Anything that you say or do in our custody can be used in a court of law. Relevant property will be confiscated to the State should you be charged, however it shall be returned in the event of an acquittal. Please come with us."

The Police Officer was courteous, Miguel had to give him that. There were two of them, one of them reading the statement from a card while the other placed him in handcuffs. He wasn't surprised, he had expected this.

He was on his doorstep, a few of his neighbors coming out to spectate his arrest. He couldn't blame them, he'd been well known locally. His vocal denunciations of regionalism, that active support by any means of the rightful Spanish government by any means necessary, loudly declared in town meetings, squares and bars. He figured it was only a matter of time before the regionalist gestapo came for him.

One of the police officers closed his door and locked it with the key Miguel had provided, a courtesy that was appreciated . They would probably ransack it later, but at least he was afforded some dignity. The other police officer walked him to the waiting police car.

"It's a shame you men are with this new State. You seem to have more decorum than most other traitors," he said as they placed him in the backseat, "arresting people for nothing more than their support for the rightful government."

The officer sighed, aged eyes looking at Miguel. "Some of us have seen enough barbarity to last us a lifetime Mr Novo" he said as he shut the car door.

title: Отказ служить
desc:
The court was closed. No Jury or spectators stood behind Lois. The small, bare courtroom held only Lois, his guards, a clerk and the judge that sat before him. Not surprising, what legitimacy did this court have anyway? The uniforms were no different from before.

"Lois Varela, you stand here accused of dereliction of duty, refusing to respect the repeated call up notices delivered to your addre-"

Lois cut in, shouting over the monotone voice of the judge. "This is a sham. I won't commit murder against my comrades, regardless of their state. I don't care what tortures you concoct to coerce me, I will wear no military uniform."

Lois glared defiantly. He'd been preparing that since he'd walked in. The Judge however stared dispassionately. "Be that as it may Mr Varela, you don't possess a special exemption from the Law. We are all subjects."

"Unjust Law is illegitimate," Lois retorted, adding "your honor" sarcastically. He had heard the fates that had befallen similar men of conviction across Spain; he had prepared himself for it. He had been lucky to have been exempted before, but he'd known it would run out eventually. He'd been silent before, he would be damned if he made no statement now.

"We won't debate the legitimacy of Galicia or its laws Mr Valera. In accordance with the emergency provisions I see no other recourse."

Louis breathed in. This was it.

"I sentence you to a suspended custodial sentence, with a conditional period of obligated labor to a strategic industry which shall be assigned in the coming days. Return the prisoner."
